notes: Package manager npm (package-lock.json, packageManager npm@11.19.1, engines npm >=11.17.0; CI: corepack enable npm + npm ci). Node: engines >=24.0.0, README 'v24 or above', CI v24.x. 'npm run dx' works on a fresh clone (pure shell script) and does: npm ci (install:npm), docker compose -f docker/development/compose.yml up -d (compose-up), prisma migrate dev via dotenv (prisma:migrate; also generates the client), prisma db seed. So the decomposed sequence is env-copy, install:npm, compose-up, prisma:migrate, seed. .env must exist before dx because prisma scripts load it via 'with:env' (dotenv -e .env -e .env.local); .env.example defaults (DB on 127.0.0.1:54320, NEXTAUTH_SECRET='secret', encryption keys, SMTP to inbucket) work without edits. 'npm run dev' compiles lingui translations then turbo dev for @documenso/remix on http://localhost:3000. 'npm run d' (README.md:136-140) = dx + translate:compile + dev in one go. README.md:132 says dx starts postgres and inbucket; the compose file also starts redis (only for the optional BullMQ jobs provider) and gotenberg (only for optional DOCX conversion, NEXT_PRIVATE_DOCUMENT_CONVERSION_URL is commented out), so they are not listed as required services. Inbucket (mail catcher, UI :9000, SMTP :2500) is recorded as mailpit. A docs 'Manual Setup' path (manual.mdx) uses npm i, your own Postgres, cp .env.example .env, npm run prisma:migrate-dev, npm run dev. readmeCommands omit the 'git clone' line (fresh clone assumed) and the alternative 'npm run d'.
